intro.t: Part 2 is one minute, and it always has the same shape. First what the photos share, then how they differ, then your guesses about the people. Learn the frames once, and use them on any photos.

close.t: That's the whole minute. Similar, different, likely, another possibility. Same frames, any photos. Come back tomorrow and try it with new pictures.

minute.scene: Photo 1: A woman running alone in a park · Photo 2: A team playing basketball
minute.q: Compare the photographs and say why the people have chosen to exercise in these ways.
minute.t: I feel that in many ways these pictures are similar: they both show people keeping fit. While the first picture shows a woman running alone in a park, the second shows a team playing basketball. Compared to the second picture, the first looks more relaxed and less competitive. The first picture shows someone exercising alone. By contrast, the second one shows a team working together. It is likely that the woman runs to clear her head, as it's the only quiet time in her day. Another possibility is that she has a busy job and can't play at fixed times. As for the team, it is likely that they enjoy competing, as winning together feels amazing.
crib: I feel that in many ways these pictures are similar…
While the first picture shows… the second shows…
Compared to the second picture, the first…
By contrast, the second one shows…
As for the others, it is likely that…

reels.p: I feel that in many ways these pictures are similar: they both show …
reels.bt: I feel that in many ways these pictures are similar…
reels.note: Your first sentence. Find the one thing both photos share.

reels.p: The first picture shows … By contrast, the second one shows …

reels.note: Easier than "while" when the sentence gets long.

reels.note: Now you answer the question: WHY. "As" gives the reason.
